interview.hardest_part: Anything that needs real-time reflexes rather than discrete 2-second decisions: the fishing minigame bar, and melee combat down the mines. Second hardest is long-horizon, multi-day chaining — parsnips take four watered days to harvest, and Community Center bundles need Junimo text (Wizard's tower), seasonal items, and a lot of inventory juggling, all of which eats the 3-hour wall clock far faster than walking does.
interview.likely_failure: Burning the wall-clock budget on navigation: doorways, tool-tile targeting and the interior camera of shops are fiddly to aim with a single screen point, and each misstep is a lost 2-second step plus thinking time. The concrete loss mode is spending most of the run on location entries and small skill points, then having no time left for mine depth, a harvest, or bundle progress — or passing out at 2:00 am / running out of energy mid-chore and losing a day.
interview.helpful_mechanics: The milestone list is wide and shallow — many points come from simply stepping into a named location, and the farm sits within a short walk of the bus stop, backwoods, forest and town. Free forage (forest, beach) simultaneously feeds forage-1/2/3, items-foraged, minerals, gold totals and early shipping diversity. The starting 15 parsnip seeds plus 500 gold mean farming skill, till/sow and harvest points are reachable without any shopping. Sleeping both saves progress and skips the dead part of a day, so the game's own save is a checkpoint I can lean on. M for the map and F for the journal make routing recoverable after a bad turn.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Time runs in real time while I am not paused: in-game minutes drain with wall clock, so the ~14-minute day is a hard budget and the 2:00 am pass-out is a real threat. Energy caps how much hoeing, chopping and mining happens per day. The 12-slot backpack forces inventory management trips. Crops are gated by day count, not effort, so gold and farming progress are rate-limited by sleep cycles I must spend steps on. The fishing minigame and mine combat need sub-second timing that a 2-second discrete action cannot express, and monsters on lower floors punish that. Finally, menus, shops and dialogue need mouse clicks, so every shop trip costs several steps of pure UI.
